rationale: A shows brief, direct reactions to TOUCH (t=8), OFFER_FOOD (t=32), and STARTLE (t=68) but ignores CALL (t=20) and PRESENT_OBJECT:PLAY_BALL (t=44), then spends long periods with attention=NONE (t=40–67, 72–95) and little spontaneous exploration. B consistently responds to TOUCH (t=8–11), CALL (t=20), OFFER_FOOD (t=32–35), PRESENT_OBJECT (t=44–53), and STARTLE/aversive focus (t=66–77), and also initiates multiple sensible, self-directed shifts (to SHELTER t=18–19, PLAY_MIRROR t=30–31, PLAY_CUBE t=54–65 and t=94–95, PLAY_CHIME t=78–83). B’s behavior forms coherent sequences and demonstrates recovery and renewed engagement after aversive events, indicating higher autonomy, adaptability, and overall apparent aliveness than A.
